symbols.name: b

symbols.name: i

symbols.name: N_n
symbols.def: Total population size \(N_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}n_{nb}\).

symbols.name: w_{nb}
symbols.def: Block weight \(w_{nb}=n_{nb}/N_n\).

symbols.name: Y_{nbi}(a)
symbols.def: Potential outcome of unit \(i\) in block \(b\) under arm \(a\).

symbols.name: Z_{nbi}
symbols.def: Assigned arm for unit \(i\) in block \(b\).

symbols.name: Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}
symbols.def: Observed response \(Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_{nbi}(Z_{nbi})\).

symbols.name: \mathcal F_{n,b-1}
symbols.def: Pre-block history containing all prior assignments and observed outcomes and the current block's baseline information.

symbols.name: m_{nba}
symbols.def: Number of units assigned to arm \(a\) in block \(b\), with \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}m_{nba}=n_{nb}\).

symbols.name: p_{nba}
symbols.def: Marginal assignment probability \(p_{nba}=m_{nba}/n_{nb}\).

symbols.name: c
symbols.def: Prespecified arm contrast \(c=(c_a)_{a\in\mathcal A}\).

symbols.name: g_{nbi}(a)
symbols.def: Past-fitted prediction for \(Y_{nbi}(a)\), evaluated before block \(b\) is randomized.

symbols.name: R_{nbi}(a)
symbols.def: Residual \(R_{nbi}(a)=Y_{nbi}(a)-g_{nbi}(a)\), fixed conditional on \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\).

symbols.name: \bar R_{nba}
symbols.def: Armwise block residual mean \(\bar R_{nba}=n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}R_{nbi}(a)\).

symbols.name: S_{nba}^2
symbols.def: Residual variance \(S_{nba}^2=(n_{nb}-1)^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}\{R_{nbi}(a)-\bar R_{nba}\}^2\).

symbols.name: \mu_{nba}
symbols.def: Centered residual marginal \(\mu_{nba}=n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}\delta_{R_{nbi}(a)-\bar R_{nba}}\).

symbols.name: \Gamma_{nb}
symbols.def: Set \(\Gamma(\mu_{nb1},\ldots,\mu_{nbK})\) of probability laws on \(\mathbb R^K\) with the stated armwise marginals.

symbols.name: J_{nb}^{-}
symbols.def: Minimum quadratic contrast cost over \(\Gamma_{nb}\).

symbols.name: J_{nb}^{+}
symbols.def: Maximum quadratic contrast cost over \(\Gamma_{nb}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal O_{nba}
symbols.def: Assigned-arm index set \(\mathcal O_{nba}=\{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}:Z_{nbi}=a\}\), whose cardinality is \(m_{nba}\) under complete-block randomization.

symbols.name: \widehat{\bar R}_{nba}
symbols.def: Assigned-arm sample mean \(\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}=m_{nba}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)
symbols.def: For \(i\in\mathcal O_{nba}\), the observable centered residual \(\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)=Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)-\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}\).

symbols.name: \widehat S_{nba}^2
symbols.def: Observable variance \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=(m_{nba}-1)^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)\}^2\) when \(m_{nba}\ge2\), with value zero when \(m_{nba}\le1\).

symbols.name: \widehat\mu_{nba}
symbols.def: Observable assigned-arm residual measure \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=m_{nba}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)}\). If \(m_{nba}=0\), set \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\).

symbols.name: \widehat J_{nb}^{-}
symbols.def: Minimum empirical transport cost formed from \(\widehat\mu_{nba}\).

symbols.name: \widehat J_{nb}^{+}
symbols.def: Maximum empirical transport cost formed from \(\widehat\mu_{nba}\).

symbols.name: \tau_n
symbols.def: Contrast average \(\tau_n=N_n^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_aY_{nbi}(a)\).

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_n
symbols.def: Predictably adjusted AIPW estimator of \(\tau_n\).

symbols.name: D_{nb}
symbols.def: Centered block contribution satisfying \(\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}D_{nb}\).

symbols.name: M_{nj}
symbols.def: Partial-sum process \(M_{nj}=\sum_{b=1}^{j}D_{nb}\) for \(j\le B_n\).

symbols.name: V_n
symbols.def: Predictable quadratic variation \(V_n=\langle M_n\rangle_{B_n}=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})\).
symbols.role: true design variance along the adaptive history

symbols.name: s_n^2
symbols.def: Primitive design scale \(s_n^2=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\).

symbols.name: \varepsilon_0
symbols.def: Common overlap constant for the uniform triangular-array class.

symbols.name: \delta_0
symbols.def: Common excess-moment exponent for the nuisance-adjusted residual arrays.

symbols.name: C_R
symbols.def: Common \((4+\delta_0)\)-moment envelope for all predictable-adjustment residuals.

symbols.name: q_n
symbols.def: Common lower arm-count sequence satisfying \(q_n\to\infty\).

symbols.name: \ell_n

symbols.name: v_0
symbols.def: Common lower predictable-quadratic-variation constant for the uniform class.

symbols.name: C_{\mathrm{ep}}

symbols.name: L_n
symbols.def: Lower endpoint of the predictable coupling envelope for \(V_n\).

symbols.name: U_n
symbols.def: Upper endpoint of the predictable coupling envelope for \(V_n\).

symbols.name: \widehat L_n
symbols.def: Plug-in lower endpoint formed from observed armwise residual marginals.

symbols.name: \widehat U_n
symbols.def: Plug-in upper endpoint formed from observed armwise residual marginals.

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: Nominal error probability.

symbols.name: z_{1-\alpha/2}
symbols.def: The \((1-\alpha/2)\)-quantile of \(\mathcal N(0,1)\).

symbols.name: \mathrm{CI}_{n,1-\alpha}
symbols.def: Wald interval centered at \(\widehat\tau_n\) and scaled by \(\widehat U_n\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak D
symbols.def: Uniform class \(\mathfrak D(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n))\) defined in \(\text{def:admissible-arrays}\).

symbols.name: \gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}
symbols.def: Joint centered residual law induced by the common unit labels in block \(b\) at the realized pre-block history.

symbols.name: \mathcal H_{n,b-1}
symbols.def: Universal tree of assignment prefixes before block \(b\); a fixed potential-outcome completion fills in the observed responses at each prefix and thereby induces the corresponding \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-history, including nodes off the ultimately realized path.

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: An assignment-prefix node at which a completion induces observed responses and the prespecified design and fitting rules are evaluated.

symbols.name: g_{nbi}^{h}(a)
symbols.def: Value produced for unit \(i\) and arm \(a\) by the fixed predictable fitting rule when the pre-block history is \(h\).

symbols.name: R_{nbi}^{h}(a)
symbols.def: Residual \(R_{nbi}^{h}(a)=Y_{nbi}(a)-g_{nbi}^{h}(a)\) at history node \(h\).

symbols.name: \bar R_{nba}^{h}
symbols.def: Mean \(\bar R_{nba}^{h}=n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}R_{nbi}^{h}(a)\).

symbols.name: \mu_{nba}^{h}
symbols.def: Centered empirical marginal of \(R_{nbi}^{h}(a)\) across \(i\in\mathcal U_{nb}\) at node \(h\).

symbols.name: m_{nba}^{h}
symbols.def: Arm-\(a\) count produced by the prespecified predictable allocation rule at node \(h\), with \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}m_{nba}^{h}=n_{nb}\).

symbols.name: (S_{nba}^{h})^2
symbols.def: Finite-population variance of \(R_{nbi}^{h}(a)\) across \(i\in\mathcal U_{nb}\) at node \(h\).

symbols.name: \Gamma_{nb}^{h}
symbols.def: The set \(\Gamma(\mu_{nb1}^{h},\ldots,\mu_{nbK}^{h})\) of convexified joint residual laws at node \(h\).

symbols.name: J_{nb}^{h,-}
symbols.def: Minimum quadratic contrast cost over \(\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\).

symbols.name: J_{nb}^{h,+}
symbols.def: Maximum quadratic contrast cost over \(\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\).

symbols.name: \boldsymbol\mu_n
symbols.def: The ex ante collection \(\boldsymbol\mu_n=(\mu_{nba}^{h})_{b\le B_n,\,h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1},\,a\in\mathcal A}\) indexed by every possible pre-block history.

symbols.name: \mathfrak R_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)
symbols.def: The Cartesian product of \(\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\) over all blocks and all possible pre-block histories.

symbols.name: \Xi_n
symbols.def: One fixed potential-outcome array together with the evaluations, at every history node, of the prespecified predictable design and fitting rules.

symbols.name: \gamma_{nb}^{\Xi,h}
symbols.def: The joint coupling induced at node \(h\) by the common unit labels in the single completion \(\Xi_n\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)
symbols.type: set of ex ante deterministic completion objects
symbols.def: History-tree compatible fixed-potential-outcome completions defined in \(\text{def:completion-class}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal P_n
symbols.type: finite set of root-to-leaf assignment paths
symbols.def: Set of complete assignment paths through the universal history tree.

symbols.name: \varpi
symbols.def: A complete assignment path through the history tree.

symbols.name: h_b(\varpi)
symbols.def: The pre-block node visited by path \(\varpi\) before block \(b\).

symbols.name: U_{nb}^{h}
symbols.def: Nodewise upper conditional-variance contribution \(U_{nb}^{h}=w_{nb}^2\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_a^2(S_{nba}^{h})^2/m_{nba}^{h}-J_{nb}^{h,-}/(n_{nb}-1)\}\), with the variances and predictable counts evaluated at \(h\).

symbols.name: Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h}
symbols.def: Conditional-variance contribution \(Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h}=w_{nb}^2\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_a^2(S_{nba}^{h})^2/m_{nba}^{h}-(n_{nb}-1)^{-1}\int(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a)^2d\gamma_{nb}^{\Xi,h}\}\) induced by completion \(\Xi_n\) at node \(h\).

symbols.name: \mathcal I_{nb}^{h}
symbols.type: finite set of deterministic nodewise couplings
symbols.def: Couplings of \(\mu_{nb1}^{h},\ldots,\mu_{nbK}^{h}\) induced by same-size unit-label matchings at node \(h\), ignoring compatibility with other history nodes.

symbols.name: \rho
symbols.def: Fixed fractional reduction used for a nodewise rectangular upper contribution or for the observable upper endpoint in the fixed-quota necessity theorem.

symbols.name: U_{nb}^{h,\rho}
symbols.def: Fixed-fraction nodewise reduction \(U_{nb}^{h,\rho}=(1-\rho)U_{nb}^{h}\).

symbols.name: U_n^{\rho}(\varpi)
symbols.def: Reduced pathwise endpoint \(U_n^{\rho}(\varpi)=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}(1-\rho)U_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi)}\).

symbols.name: \Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)
symbols.def: Normalized global compatibility gap defined in \(\text{def:completion-gap}\).

symbols.name: \Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)
symbols.def: Normalized worst single-node multi-index integrality gap defined in \(\text{def:completion-gap}\).

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: Endpoint-rate exponent \(\kappa=\frac{2+\delta_0}{6(4+\delta_0)}\).

symbols.name: r_n
symbols.def: Endpoint-error envelope \(r_n=q_n^{-\kappa}\), which tends to zero.

symbols.name: \Phi
symbols.def: Cumulative distribution function of \(\mathcal N(0,1)\).

assumptions.condition: Conditional on baseline information, the array \(\{Y_{nbi}(a):b\le B_n,\ i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\ a\in\mathcal A\}\) is nonrandom under the assignment law.
The fixed-count vector \((m_{nba})_{a\in\mathcal A}\) is \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-measurable for every \(n\) and \(b\).

novel.justification: This is an explicit fixed-count complete-block design restriction of the paper. It is implementable in predictably batched platform experiments that update integer arm quotas after each completed batch and then use uniform complete randomization within the next batch; minimum cell sizes and capacity caps can be enforced directly by the quota rule. Li and Zhao's broader block-adaptive framework is not cited as supplying this restriction.

assumptions.condition: Conditional on \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\), \((Z_{nbi})_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}\) is uniform over assignments having exactly \(m_{nba}\) units in every arm \(a\in\mathcal A\).

standard.name: Complete randomization within a predictable block

assumptions.condition: The array \((g_{nbi}(a))_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\,a\in\mathcal A}\) is \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-measurable for every \(n\) and \(b\).
The predictable arm fractions satisfy \(\varepsilon_0\le p_{nba}\le1-(K-1)\varepsilon_0\) almost surely for every \(n\), \(b\), and \(a\).
The predictable counts satisfy \(\min_{b\le B_n,\,a\in\mathcal A}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) almost surely for every \(n\), where the deterministic lower-count envelope obeys \(q_n\to\infty\).
The design leverage satisfies \(\max_{b\le B_n}\{w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\}/s_n^2\le\ell_n\) for every \(n\).
The nuisance-adjusted residual arrays satisfy \(\sup_{n,b,a}\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{\mathcal F_{n,b-1}}n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}|R_{nbi}(a)|^{4+\delta_0}\le C_R\).
The predictable quadratic variation satisfies \(V_n\ge v_0s_n^2\) almost surely for every \(n\).

novel.justification: This common finite-population condition excludes asymptotically deterministic contrasts while allowing heterogeneous residual couplings; it holds, for example, when each root-to-leaf path contains a fixed share of blocks with residual contrast variance bounded below relative to \(s_n^2\).

assumptions.condition: For every \(\eta>0\), the predictable quadratic variation stabilizes at its deterministic design expectation uniformly over the common-parameter class: \[\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}\Pr_{\mathbb D}\left(\left|\frac{V_n}{E_{\mathbb D}V_n}-1\right|>\eta\right)\longrightarrow0.\]

novel.justification: standard: predictable-variation stabilization for a martingale triangular array

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak D(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n))\)
definitions.construction:
\[
\mathfrak D(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n))=\left\{(Y_{nbi}(a),Z_{nbi},m_{nba},g_{nbi}(a))_{n\ge1,\,b\le B_n,\,i\in\mathcal U_{nb},\,a\in\mathcal A}:\begin{array}{l}K\text{ is fixed, }q_n\to\infty,\ \ell_n\to0,\text{ and every member-property assumption listed below holds for all }n;\\ \varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R,v_0,(q_n),(\ell_n)\text{ are the same displayed constants and deterministic envelopes for every array}\end{array}\right\}.
\]

definitions.name: \(\widehat{\bar R}_{nba},\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a),\widehat S_{nba}^2,\widehat\mu_{nba}\)
definitions.construction:
For \(\mathcal O_{nba}=\{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}:Z_{nbi}=a\}\) of observed size \(|\mathcal O_{nba}|=m_{nba}\), define
\[
\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)\},\qquad \widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)=Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)-\widehat{\bar R}_{nba},
\]
\[
\widehat\mu_{nba}=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)},\qquad \widehat S_{nba}^2=\frac1{m_{nba}-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)\}^2.
\]
Set \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\) and \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=0\) when \(m_{nba}=0\), and set \(\widehat S_{nba}^2=0\) when \(m_{nba}=1\). These total conventions are inactive for the endpoint theorem for all sufficiently large \(n\), because \(\min_{b,a}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) and \(q_n\to\infty\).

definitions.name: \([\widehat L_n,\widehat U_n]\)
definitions.construction: Using only the assigned-arm measures and sample variances from \(\text{def:observed-residual-margins}\), define \[\widehat L_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2\widehat S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}-\frac{\widehat J_{nb}^{+}}{n_{nb}-1}\right\},\qquad \widehat U_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2\widehat S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}-\frac{\widehat J_{nb}^{-}}{n_{nb}-1}\right\}.\]

definitions.name: Two-arm sorting map
definitions.construction: For \(K=2\) and \(c=(1,-1)/\sqrt2\), let \(F_{nb,a}^{-1}\) be the quantile function of \(\mu_{nba}\) and compute \[J_{nb}^{-}=\frac12\int_0^1\{F_{nb,1}^{-1}(u)-F_{nb,2}^{-1}(u)\}^2\,du,\qquad J_{nb}^{+}=\frac12\int_0^1\{F_{nb,1}^{-1}(u)-F_{nb,2}^{-1}(1-u)\}^2\,du.\]

definitions.name: Fixed-\(K\) empirical transportation program
definitions.construction: Feed the observable measures \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=m_{nba}^{-1}\sum_{i_a\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi_a}^{c}(a)}\) from \(\text{def:observed-residual-margins}\) into the finite program. When every \(m_{nba}>0\), optimize over variables \(\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\ge0\), indexed by \((i_1,\ldots,i_K)\in\prod_{a=1}^K\mathcal O_{nba}\), the objective \[\sum_{i_1\in\mathcal O_{nb1}}\cdots\sum_{i_K\in\mathcal O_{nbK}}\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\left\{\sum_{a=1}^Kc_a\widehat R_{nbi_a}^{c}(a)\right\}^2\] subject, for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and every \(i_a\in\mathcal O_{nba}\), to the exact marginal constraints \[\sum_{(i_{a'})_{a'\ne a}\in\prod_{a'\ne a}\mathcal O_{nba'}}\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}=\frac1{m_{nba}}.\] The minimum is \(\widehat J_{nb}^{-}\) and the maximum is \(\widehat J_{nb}^{+}\). If an arm sample is empty, represent its convention \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\) by one artificial zero atom of mass one and solve the same marginal-coupling program; the admissible class never invokes this branch.

definitions.name: Worked validation: the \(\{-1,-1,1,1\}\) coupling witness
definitions.construction: Take one block of size \(n_{nb}=4\), \(K=2\), the unnormalized contrast \(c=(1,-1)\), and both centered marginal lists equal to \(\{-1,-1,1,1\}\). Direct substitution into the two-arm sorting costs gives \[J_{nb}^{-}=\frac14\{(-1+1)^2+(-1+1)^2+(1-1)^2+(1-1)^2\}=0\] under equal-rank pairing and \[J_{nb}^{+}=\frac14\{(-1-1)^2+(-1-1)^2+(1+1)^2+(1+1)^2\}=4\] under reverse-rank pairing. Substitution into \(\text{def:qv-envelope}\) therefore gives \(U_n-L_n=w_{nb}^2(J_{nb}^{+}-J_{nb}^{-})/(n_{nb}-1)=4w_{nb}^2/3>0\) for this single block. Under the normalized contrast \(c=(1,-1)/\sqrt2\), both costs and the width are divided by two. This is a direct arithmetic validation of sorting direction and endpoint signs, not a theorem contribution.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak R_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\)
definitions.construction: For the ex ante history-tree margin system \(\boldsymbol\mu_n=(\mu_{nba}^{h})_{b\le B_n,\,h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1},\,a\in\mathcal A}\), set \(\Gamma_{nb}^{h}=\Gamma(\mu_{nb1}^{h},\ldots,\mu_{nbK}^{h})\), define \[J_{nb}^{h,-}=\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma_{nb}^{h}}\int(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a)^2d\gamma,\qquad J_{nb}^{h,+}=\sup_{\gamma\in\Gamma_{nb}^{h}}\int(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a)^2d\gamma,\] define \[U_{nb}^{h}=w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2(S_{nba}^{h})^2}{m_{nba}^{h}}-\frac{J_{nb}^{h,-}}{n_{nb}-1}\right\},\] and let \(\mathfrak R_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=\prod_{b=1}^{B_n}\prod_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1}}\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\). The Cartesian product permits a separate convexified coupling at every history node.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\)
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=\left\{\Xi_n=\left((Y_{nbi}(a))_{b,i,a},(m_{nba}^{h})_{b,h,a},(g_{nbi}^{h}(a))_{b,h,i,a}\right):\begin{array}{l}(Y_{nbi}(a))_{b,i,a}\text{ is fixed before randomization};\\ (m_{nba}^{h})_{a\in\mathcal A}\text{ and }(g_{nbi}^{h}(a))_{i,a}\text{ are the evaluations of the same prespecified predictable allocation and fitting rules at every }h;\\ \text{for every }b\le B_n\text{ and }h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1},\ R_{nbi}^{h}(a)=Y_{nbi}(a)-g_{nbi}^{h}(a)\text{ has centered margins }\mu_{nba}^{h};\\ \gamma_{nb}^{\Xi,h}=n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}\delta_{(R_{nbi}^{h}(1)-\bar R_{nb1}^{h},\ldots,R_{nbi}^{h}(K)-\bar R_{nbK}^{h})}\in\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\end{array}\right\}.\] Thus one member fixes common unit labels and all potential outcomes before assignment and induces the counts, fitted values, residual margins, feasible couplings, and transport endpoints at every node, including nodes off the realized path.

definitions.name: \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n),\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n),U_n^{\rho}(\varpi)\)
definitions.construction:
For \(\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\), let \(Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h}\) be its nodewise conditional-variance contribution. With the predictable block weight already included in \(U_{nb}^{h}\) and \(Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h}\), define the normalized root-to-leaf compatibility gap
\[
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=\inf_{\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)}\ \sup_{\varpi\in\mathcal P_n}\frac1{s_n^2}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}\left\{U_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi)}-Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h_b(\varpi)}\right\}.
\]
Define the single-node multi-index integrality diagnostic
\[
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=\sup_{b\le B_n,\,h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1}}\frac{w_{nb}^2}{s_n^2(n_{nb}-1)}\left[\inf_{\gamma\in\mathcal I_{nb}^{h}}\int\left(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma-J_{nb}^{h,-}\right].
\]
For a fixed \(\rho\in(0,1)\), define the reduced nodewise contribution \(U_{nb}^{h,\rho}=(1-\rho)U_{nb}^{h}\) and the corresponding root-to-leaf endpoint
\[
U_n^{\rho}(\varpi)=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}U_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi),\rho}.
\]
The two gaps and \(U_n^{\rho}(\varpi)\) are retained only for the unresolved global history-tree compatibility problem; the fixed-fraction necessity result for uniform inference is certified separately by an explicit nonadaptive fixed-quota subclass.

definitions.name: Residual history-tree integer-flow handle
definitions.construction: The fixed-fraction necessity direction for uniform inference is settled by the explicit nonadaptive fixed-quota subclass in \(\text{thm:fixed-fraction-upper-endpoint-necessity}\). The remaining handle concerns only global adaptive-history compatibility: represent one ex ante sequence \((\Xi_n)_{n\ge1}\), with \(\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\) and its entire induced triangular experiment-analysis array in \(\mathfrak D\), as a history-tree integer multi-index flow with common unit labels. Enforce prefix consistency by backward induction and compare its root-to-leaf objective with \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\). Use rational replication at an isolated node to measure \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\), then characterize the additional loss caused by sharing one fixed potential-outcome array and one predictable fitting rule across incompatible branches while preserving membership in \(\mathfrak D\).

statements.statement: For every array in \(\mathfrak D\), \((M_{nj},\mathcal F_{n,j})_{j\le B_n}\) is a martingale and \[E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})=w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}-\frac1{n_{nb}-1}\int\left(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}\right\},\] where \(\gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}\in\Gamma_{nb}\) is the joint centered residual coupling in block \(b\). At every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1}\), the conditional variance range over \(\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\) has endpoints obtained from \(J_{nb}^{h,+}\) and \(J_{nb}^{h,-}\), and both endpoints are attained in that node's convexified coupling set. Evaluating these nodewise endpoints along the realized pre-block histories yields the predictable pathwise containment \(V_n\in[L_n,U_n]\). The interval is exact in the rectangular convexified history-tree relaxation \(\mathfrak R_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\); this theorem does not assert that one \(\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\) simultaneously realizes the selected optimizers across the tree. When \(B_n=1\) and \(g_{nbi}(a)=0\), the result reduces to the static quadratic MOT variance formula of Gao, Ge, and Qian. When \(B_n\ge2\) and counts respond to earlier outcomes, \([L_n,U_n]\) is a sum of pre-block-measurable random endpoints rather than one static MOT functional, and the claim does not condition on \(\mathcal F_{n,B_n}\).

statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\) and a block \(b\), and abbreviate \(N=n_{nb}\), \(m_a=m_{nba}\), \(p_a=m_a/N\), \(R_i(a)=R_{nbi}(a)\), and
\[
x_i(a)=R_i(a)-\bar R_{nba}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:fixed\text{-}potential\text{-}outcomes}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:predictable\text{-}adjustment}\), the lists \((x_i(a))_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}\) are fixed conditional on \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\). By \(\mathrm{ass:predictable\text{-}counts}\), the positive integers \(m_a\) are fixed under the same conditioning. Finally, \(\mathrm{ass:complete\text{-}block\text{-}randomization}\) gives, with \(I_i^a=\mathbf 1\{Z_{nbi}=a\}\),
\[
E(I_i^a\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})=\frac{m_a}{N}=p_a.
\tag{1}
\]
Consequently each arm sample mean is conditionally unbiased for its finite-population mean. The definition in \(\mathrm{def:block\text{-}martingale}\) and (1) therefore give
\[
E(D_{nb}\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=w_{nb}\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_a
\left\{\frac1{m_a}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}p_aR_i(a)-\bar R_{nba}\right\}=0.
\tag{2}
\]
The increment \(D_{nb}\) is measurable after block \(b\) has been randomized, and the residual-moment member property of \(\mathfrak D\) makes it square integrable. Thus \(M_{nj}=\sum_{b\le j}D_{nb}\) is adapted, integrable, and has zero conditional increments by (2); hence \((M_{nj},\mathcal F_{n,j})_{j\le B_n}\) is a martingale.

We next calculate the conditional variance. Complete randomization gives, for distinct units \(i\ne k\),
\[
E(I_i^aI_k^a\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=\frac{m_a(m_a-1)}{N(N-1)},
\qquad
E(I_i^aI_k^{a'}\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=\frac{m_am_{a'}}{N(N-1)}\quad(a\ne a'),
\tag{3}
\]
whereas \(I_i^aI_i^{a'}=0\) when \(a\ne a'\). Since \(\sum_i x_i(a)=0\), expansion using (1)--(3) yields
\[
\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\frac1{m_a}\sum_i I_i^aR_i(a)\middle|\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\right)
=\left(\frac1{m_a}-\frac1N\right)S_{nba}^2,
\tag{4}
\]
and, for \(a\ne a'\),
\[
\operatorname{Cov}\!\left(\frac1{m_a}\sum_iI_i^aR_i(a),
\frac1{m_{a'}}\sum_iI_i^{a'}R_i(a')\middle|\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\right)
=-\frac{S_{nb,aa'}}N,
\tag{5}
\]
where
\[
S_{nb,aa'}=\frac1{N-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}x_i(a)x_i(a').
\]
Indeed, (4) is the usual expansion into diagonal and distinct-label terms using the first formula in (3), and (5) follows from the second formula in (3) together with
\(\sum_{i\ne k}x_i(a)x_k(a')=-\sum_i x_i(a)x_i(a')\).

Using (4)--(5) and then collecting diagonal and off-diagonal terms gives, equation by equation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})}{w_{nb}^2}
&=\sum_a\frac{c_a^2S_{nba}^2}{m_a}
-\frac1N\left\{\sum_a c_a^2S_{nba}^2
+2\sum_{a<a'}c_ac_{a'}S_{nb,aa'}\right\}\\
&=\sum_a\frac{c_a^2S_{nba}^2}{m_a}
-\frac1{N(N-1)}\sum_i\left\{\sum_a c_ax_i(a)\right\}^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
Define the common-label joint centered residual law
\[
\gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}
=\frac1N\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}
\delta_{(x_i(1),\ldots,x_i(K))}.
\]
Its \(a\)-th marginal is exactly \(\mu_{nba}\), so \(\gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}\in\Gamma_{nb}\). Substitution in (6) proves
\[
E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=w_{nb}^2\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2S_{nba}^2}{m_{nba}}
-\frac1{n_{nb}-1}\int\left(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a\right)^2
d\gamma_{nb}^{\mathrm{true}}\right\}.
\tag{7}
\]

Fix now a history node \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1}\). Each margin \(\mu_{nba}^h\) has finite support. Hence \(\Gamma_{nb}^h\) is a nonempty compact finite-dimensional transportation polytope: nonemptiness follows from the product coupling, closedness from the finitely many marginal equalities, and boundedness from nonnegativity and total mass one. The quadratic cost is a linear continuous functional of the coupling variable. It therefore attains its minimum \(J_{nb}^{h,-}\) and maximum \(J_{nb}^{h,+}\); because the polytope is convex, its image is the whole interval \([J_{nb}^{h,-},J_{nb}^{h,+}]\). The cost enters (7) with coefficient \(-w_{nb}^2/(n_{nb}-1)\). Thus the lower conditional-variance endpoint is obtained from \(J_{nb}^{h,+}\), and the upper endpoint is obtained from \(J_{nb}^{h,-}\), with both attained in the nodewise convexified coupling set.

These endpoints are nonnegative. Indeed, for any \(\gamma\in\Gamma_{nb}^h\), Cauchy--Schwarz, \(p_{nba}^h=m_{nba}^h/n_{nb}\), and \(\sum_ap_{nba}^h=1\) give
\[
\left(\sum_ac_ax_a\right)^2
=\left(\sum_a\frac{c_ax_a}{\sqrt{p_{nba}^h}}\sqrt{p_{nba}^h}\right)^2
\le\sum_a\frac{c_a^2x_a^2}{p_{nba}^h}.
\]
Since
\(\int x_a^2d\mu_{nba}^h=(n_{nb}-1)(S_{nba}^h)^2/n_{nb}\), integration implies
\[
\frac1{n_{nb}-1}\int\left(\sum_ac_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma
\le\sum_a\frac{c_a^2(S_{nba}^h)^2}{m_{nba}^h}.
\tag{8}
\]

By \(\mathrm{def:history\text{-}tree\text{-}rectangular\text{-}relaxation}\), a coupling may be selected independently at every history node. Along any fixed root-to-leaf path, the Minkowski sum of the nodewise real intervals is the interval whose endpoints are the sums of the respective nodewise endpoints. On the realized path, the common-label coupling is feasible at every visited node by (7). Summing (7) over visited blocks and using \(\mathrm{def:qv\text{-}envelope}\) therefore gives the predictable pathwise containment
\[
V_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})\in[L_n,U_n].
\tag{9}
\]
Every summand and endpoint in (9) is measurable before its own block is randomized. The argument never conditions on \(\mathcal F_{n,B_n}\). The Cartesian-product construction proves exactness in \(\mathfrak R_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\), while \(\mathrm{def:completion\text{-}class}\) shows why this says nothing about whether a single globally consistent \(\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\) realizes independently selected optimizers at all nodes.

The requested two-block kill test is contained in (2). Even if the second-block count vector is an arbitrary \(\mathcal F_{n,1}\)-measurable function of first-block assignments and outcomes,
\[
E(D_{n1}D_{n2})
=E\{D_{n1}E(D_{n2}\mid\mathcal F_{n,1})\}=0.
\tag{10}
\]
Here is an exact enumeration in the smallest convenient adaptive-quota example. Take two arms, \(c=(1,-1)/\sqrt2\), and zero adjustment. In block one use the common two-label residual list \((-1,1)\) and quota \((1,1)\). There are two assignments: according as arm one receives the label \(1\) or \(-1\),
\[
D_{n1}=\sqrt2w_{n1}\quad\text{or}\quad D_{n1}=-\sqrt2w_{n1}.
\]
After the positive value choose the predictable block-two quota \((1,2)\); after the negative value choose \((2,1)\). Give both arms in block two the common residual list \((-1,0,1)\). Put \(d=3w_{n2}/(2\sqrt2)\). Under quota \((1,2)\), the three equiprobable arm-one singleton choices give
\[
D_{n2}\in\{-d,0,d\};
\]
under quota \((2,1)\), the three equiprobable omitted-singleton choices give
\[
D_{n2}\in\{d,0,-d\}.
\]
Thus all six assignment sequences have been enumerated, each history has conditional block-two mean zero, and their cross-product average is
\[
\frac12\left[\sqrt2w_{n1}\frac{-d+0+d}{3}
-\sqrt2w_{n1}\frac{d+0-d}{3}\right]=0.
\tag{11}
\]
Hence no unidentified cross-block covariance survives predictable conditioning. Finally, when \(B_n=1\) and \(g_{nbi}(a)=0\), the residuals equal the potential outcomes, and direct substitution into (7) is exactly the stated static quadratic multi-marginal-transport variance formula.

statements.statement: The constructions in \(\text{def:twoarm-sorting}\) equal \(J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(J_{nb}^{+}\) for \(K=2\). For each fixed \(K\), feeding the observable assigned-arm measures \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=m_{nba}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{\widehat R_{nbi}^{c}(a)}\) into the finite primal programs in \(\text{def:fixed-k-lp}\) attains \(\widehat J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(\widehat J_{nb}^{+}\), and their Kantorovich duals have the same values. These are exact convexified empirical endpoints. At any single history node, every rational optimal plan is realized by a deterministic fixed-potential-outcome block completion after finite replication of that node's armwise lists, so its LP endpoints are asymptotically nodewise completion-attainable as block sizes grow. No same-size integrality assertion for \(K>2\), and no cross-history assertion that one \(\Xi_n\) realizes independently chosen nodewise plans, is made.

statements.proof_tex:
For \(K=2\) and \(c=(1,-1)/\sqrt2\), the identity
\[
\frac12(x-y)^2=\frac12x^2+\frac12y^2-xy
\tag{1}
\]
shows that the two marginal square terms do not depend on the coupling. The cited rearrangement result \(\mathrm{lem:twoarm\text{-}rearrangement\text{-}extrema}\) says that equal-rank pairing maximizes \(E(XY)\), whereas reverse-rank pairing minimizes it. By (1), equal-rank pairing therefore minimizes the quadratic cost and reverse-rank pairing maximizes it. This proves the two formulas in \(\mathrm{def:twoarm\text{-}sorting}\).

For general fixed \(K\), label every atom of every observed empirical margin, even when two labels carry the same numerical residual. A coupling of the labeled empirical measures assigns a mass \(\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\ge0\) to each tuple
\((i_1,\ldots,i_K)\in\prod_{a=1}^K\mathcal O_{nba}\). Its \(a\)-th marginal is \(\widehat\mu_{nba}\) if and only if
\[
\sum_{(i_{a'})_{a'\ne a}\in\prod_{a'\ne a}\mathcal O_{nba'}}
\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}=\frac1{m_{nba}}
\tag{2}
\]
for every \(a\) and every \(i_a\in\mathcal O_{nba}\). Thus the feasible arrays in \(\mathrm{def:fixed\text{-}k\text{-}lp}\) are exactly all couplings of the empirical margins, and the displayed LP objective is exactly
\[
\int\left(\sum_{a=1}^Kc_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma.
\]
The feasible set is nonempty because it contains the product coupling, and it is a compact polytope because (2), nonnegativity, and total mass one define a closed bounded subset of a finite-dimensional space. The linear objective consequently attains its minimum and maximum, which are respectively \(\widehat J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(\widehat J_{nb}^{+}\) by \(\mathrm{def:transport\text{-}values}\). The cited finite multi-marginal Kantorovich duality result \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}mot\text{-}kantorovich\text{-}duality}\) equates the minimum with its finite dual. Applying the same result to the negative cost and multiplying both primal and dual values by \(-1\) proves the corresponding equality for the maximum. Hence both programs give exact convexified empirical endpoints.

It remains to prove the replication assertion, which is specific to this proposition. The constraints in (2) have rational coefficients and rational right-hand sides. A linear functional on a nonempty polytope has an optimal face containing an extreme point; every extreme point of this rational polytope is rational because its coordinates solve a full-rank subsystem of the active rational equalities. Thus a rational optimal plan exists. More generally, let \(\pi\) be any rational optimal plan. Put \(N=\sum_am_{nba}=n_{nb}\), and choose an integer \(L\) divisible by \(N\), by every \(m_{nba}\), and by every denominator occurring among the finitely many values \(\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}\). Create
\[
L\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}
\]
replicated units of joint type \((i_1,\ldots,i_K)\). These multiplicities are nonnegative integers and sum to \(L\). By (2), the arm-\(a\) label \(i_a\) occurs exactly
\[
\sum_{(i_{a'})_{a'\ne a}}L\pi_{i_1\ldots i_K}
=\frac{L}{m_{nba}}
\tag{3}
\]
times. Therefore, within arm \(a\), every label is replicated by the integer factor \(L/m_{nba}\), and the empirical joint law on the replicated common unit labels is exactly \(\pi\). Set the replicated complete-randomization quota to \(m_{nba}'=(L/N)m_{nba}\); these are positive integers, preserve the original arm fractions, and sum to \(L\). Assigning to each replicated unit the corresponding centered armwise residual values, and choosing fixed potential outcomes and nodewise predictable fitted values whose difference equals those residuals, realizes the plan at that single history node. Repeating the construction at integer multiples of \(L\) gives nodewise completion attainability along growing replicated block sizes. The construction neither retains the original unreplicated block size nor enforces compatibility with any other history node, exactly as the proposition states.

As the smallest arithmetic stress test, take both centered lists to be \(\{-1,-1,1,1\}\). For the unnormalized contrast \((1,-1)\), equal-rank pairing makes the squared contrast identically zero, while reverse-rank pairing makes it identically four. Hence the two costs are \(0\) and \(4\), and for a block of size four the associated envelope width is
\[
\frac{4w_{nb}^2}{4-1}>0.
\]
For the normalized contrast \((1,-1)/\sqrt2\), both costs and this width are divided by two. This verifies both the endpoint ordering and nontrivial width.

statements.statement: For every arm and block, form the observable assigned-arm measure \(\widehat\mu_{nba}=m_{nba}^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal O_{nba}}\delta_{Y_{nbi}^{\mathrm{obs}}-g_{nbi}(a)-\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}}\), centered by the observed assigned-arm residual mean \(\widehat{\bar R}_{nba}\), and feed exactly these measures into \(\widehat J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(\widehat J_{nb}^{+}\) and the plug-in envelope. There is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{ep}}<\infty\), depending only on \(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R\), such that for every \(n\), \[\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}E_{\mathbb D}\left[1\wedge\frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}\right]\le C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n.\] Consequently, for every \(\eta>0\), \[\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}\Pr_{\mathbb D}\left(\frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}>\eta\right)\le\frac{C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n}{1\wedge\eta}\longrightarrow0.\] The same bound, without the factor two implicit in the displayed sum, holds for the normalized Hausdorff distance between \([\widehat L_n,\widehat U_n]\) and \([L_n,U_n]\). Probability and expectation are over the original sequential randomization. The inequalities hold uniformly over pre-block histories generated by arrays in the common-parameter class, use observable assigned-arm centering throughout, and do not condition on \(\mathcal F_{n,B_n}\) or freeze the realized final counts.

statements.proof_tex:
Put \(r=4+\delta_0\), and condition on an arbitrary \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\)-history. The counts, fitting values, potential outcomes, and residual lists used below are then fixed. For an arm \(a\), write
\[
X_i=R_{nbi}(a)-\bar R_{nba},\qquad N=n_{nb},\qquad m=m_{nba}.
\]
Jensen's inequality and \(\mathrm{ass:residual\text{-}moments}\) imply
\[
\frac1N\sum_i|X_i|^r
\le2^{r-1}\left\{\frac1N\sum_i|R_{nbi}(a)|^r+|\bar R_{nba}|^r\right\}
\le2^rC_R.
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:consistency\text{-}no\text{-}interference}\), the residual observed on a label assigned to arm \(a\) is \(R_{nbi}(a)\). By \(\mathrm{ass:complete\text{-}block\text{-}randomization}\), those labels form a simple random sample without replacement of size \(m\) from the \(N\) labels.

We first derive a finite-population transport bound. Define the population-centered sample and population measures
\[
\nu=\frac1m\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}\delta_{X_i},
\qquad
\mu=\frac1N\sum_i\delta_{X_i}.
\]
For \(T>0\), clip both measures to \([-T,T]\), partition that interval into \(H\) cells of length at most \(2T/H\), and project every cell to one representative. If \(P_h\) and \(\widehat P_h\) are the population and sample masses of cell \(h\), the first- and second-order inclusion probabilities of simple random sampling give
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\widehat P_h\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=\frac{N-m}{m(N-1)}P_h(1-P_h)\le\frac1{2m}.
\]
Therefore Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
E\left(\sum_{h=1}^H|\widehat P_h-P_h|\middle|\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\right)
\le\frac{H}{\sqrt{2m}}.
\tag{2}
\]
Match projected mass within each cell and move unmatched clipped mass by distance at most \(2T\). The within-cell contribution is at most \(4T^2/H^2\), and the unmatched contribution is at most a constant times \(T^2\sum_h|\widehat P_h-P_h|\). The population clipping cost is bounded using (1) and
\(X_i^2\mathbf1\{|X_i|>T\}\le |X_i|^rT^{-(r-2)}\). The conditional expected sample clipping cost equals the population clipping cost by the first-order inclusion probability. Combining these observations with (1)--(2) and the triangle inequality for \(W_2\) gives a constant \(C\), depending only on \(r\) and \(C_R\), such that
\[
E\{W_2^2(\nu,\mu)\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le C\left(\frac{T^2}{H^2}+\frac{T^2H}{\sqrt m}+T^{-(r-2)}\right).
\tag{3}
\]
Choose \(H=\lceil m^{1/6}\rceil\) and \(T=m^{1/(3r)}\). Enlarging \(C\) to absorb the ceiling, every term in (3) is at most \(Cm^{-\beta}\), where
\[
\beta=\frac{r-2}{3r}.
\tag{4}
\]

The observable measure \(\widehat\mu_{nba}\) is obtained from \(\nu\) by translation through minus the sample mean \(\bar X_S=m^{-1}\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}X_i\). Because \(N^{-1}\sum_iX_i=0\), the exact simple-random-sampling covariance identity gives
\[
E(\bar X_S^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=\left(\frac1m-\frac1N\right)S_{nba}^2\le\frac{C}{m},
\tag{5}
\]
where the last inequality follows from (1). Translation by a scalar has squared quadratic-transport cost equal to the squared scalar. The triangle inequality for \(W_2\), (3)--(5), and \(\beta<1\) therefore imply
\[
E\{W_2^2(\widehat\mu_{nba},\mu_{nba})\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le Cm_{nba}^{-\beta}.
\tag{6}
\]

For the variance term, write
\[
\overline{X^2}_S=\frac1m\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}X_i^2,
\qquad
\overline{X^2}=\frac1N\sum_iX_i^2.
\]
The same sampling covariance identity applied to the list \((X_i^2)_i\), followed by (1), gives
\[
E\{|\overline{X^2}_S-\overline{X^2}|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le\left\{\left(\frac1m-\frac1N\right)
\frac1{N-1}\sum_i(X_i^2-\overline{X^2})^2\right\}^{1/2}
\le Cm^{-1/2}.
\tag{7}
\]
Equations (5), (7), and
\[
\widehat S_{nba}^2=\frac{m}{m-1}(\overline{X^2}_S-\bar X_S^2),
\qquad
S_{nba}^2=\frac{N}{N-1}\overline{X^2}
\]
show, for \(m,N\ge2\), that
\[
E\{|\widehat S_{nba}^2-S_{nba}^2|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le Cm_{nba}^{-1/2}.
\tag{8}
\]
Here we also used \(|m/(m-1)-1|\le2/m\), \(|N/(N-1)-1|\le2/N\), and the uniform second-moment consequence of (1). All constants in (1)--(8) are history-uniform.

We next prove continuity of both multi-marginal endpoints. For every arm, take an optimal quadratic coupling of \(\mu_{nba}\) and \(\widehat\mu_{nba}\). Because the measures have finite support, these pairwise couplings admit finite conditional kernels. Starting from any \(\gamma\in\Gamma_{nb}\), draw the empirical-margin coordinates conditionally independently given the corresponding population coordinates. If \(X\) has law \(\gamma\) and \(Y\) is the resulting vector, then the margins of \(Y\) are the empirical margins and
\(E(X_a-Y_a)^2=W_2^2(\mu_{nba},\widehat\mu_{nba})\). By \(\mathrm{ass:contrast\text{-}normalization}\) and Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
\begin{aligned}
|E(c^\top X)^2-E(c^\top Y)^2|
&\le\{E(c^\top(X-Y))^2\}^{1/2}
\{E(c^\top(X+Y))^2\}^{1/2}\\
&\le\left\{\sum_aW_2^2(\mu_{nba},\widehat\mu_{nba})\right\}^{1/2}
\left\{2\sum_a(EX_a^2+EY_a^2)\right\}^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
Apply (9) first to a population optimizer and then, with the roles reversed, to an empirical optimizer. Existence follows from compactness of the finite coupling polytopes. Conditional Cauchy--Schwarz, (1), (6), and the corresponding uniform expected second-moment bound for the empirical margins yield, for either sign,
\[
E\{|\widehat J_{nb}^{\pm}-J_{nb}^{\pm}|\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\}
\le C\left(\min_a m_{nba}\right)^{-\beta/2}.
\tag{10}
\]
No uniqueness of an optimizer is required.

Let \(t_{nb}=w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\), so \(\sum_bt_{nb}=s_n^2\). Executed overlap gives \(m_{nba}^{-1}\le(\varepsilon_0n_{nb})^{-1}\), and \((n_{nb}-1)^{-1}\le2n_{nb}^{-1}\) whenever \(n_{nb}\ge2\). Combining (8), (10), and the definitions of the oracle and empirical endpoints, summing absolute block errors, and applying the tower property along the original adaptive filtration gives, whenever all arm counts are at least two,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}
E_{\mathbb D}\frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}
&\le\frac{C}{s_n^2}\sum_bt_{nb}
\left(q_n^{-1/2}+q_n^{-\beta/2}\right)\\
&\le Cq_n^{-\kappa},
\qquad
\kappa=\frac\beta2=\frac{2+\delta_0}{6(4+\delta_0)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
There is no union bound over blocks or histories in (11). At block \(b\), the predictable counts and fitted values are fixed only at its pre-block history; the conditional bounds above hold uniformly at that history, and the tower property integrates it out.

If some arm count is less than two, \(\min_{b,a}m_{nba}\ge q_n\) implies \(q_n<2\). The truncated loss is at most one, whereas
\(1\le2^\kappa q_n^{-\kappa}\). Thus, after increasing \(C\) by the universal factor \(2^\kappa\), the truncated version of (11) holds for every \(n\), including the total-convention cases. We have therefore proved
\[
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}E_{\mathbb D}\left[1\wedge
\frac{|\widehat L_n-L_n|+|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}\right]
\le C_{\mathrm{ep}}q_n^{-\kappa}=C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n,
\tag{12}
\]
where \(C_{\mathrm{ep}}\) depends only on \(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R\).

For a nonnegative random variable \(X\),
\(\mathbf1\{X>\eta\}\le(1\wedge X)/(1\wedge\eta)\). Apply this inequality to the normalized summed endpoint error in (12) to obtain the stated probability bound. The Hausdorff distance between two real intervals is
\(\max\{|\widehat L_n-L_n|,|\widehat U_n-U_n|\}\), which is no larger than the summed endpoint error, proving the last bound with the same constant. Finally, \(q_n\to\infty\) and \(\kappa>0\) imply \(r_n\to0\). Every probability and expectation above is under the original sequential randomization law; only pre-block conditional expectations were used, never conditioning on \(\mathcal F_{n,B_n}\) or freezing final adaptive counts.

statements.statement: For every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), assume in addition that \(\mathrm{ass:qv\text{-}stabilization}\) holds uniformly for the displayed common-parameter class \(\mathfrak D\). Then \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{\tau_n\in\mathrm{CI}_{n,1-\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha.\] More precisely, the common leverage envelope \(\ell_n\to0\), the common residual-moment envelope \((\delta_0,C_R)\), the finite-population nondegeneracy condition \(V_n\ge v_0s_n^2\), and uniform predictable-QV stabilization imply \((\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n)/\sqrt{V_n}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\) uniformly over \(\mathfrak D\). The exact-envelope theorem gives \(V_n\le U_n\) pathwise, and the explicit bound \(C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n=o(1)\) permits \(U_n\) to be replaced by \(\widehat U_n\). No conditioning on the terminal adaptive path is required.
statements.justification: The theorem converts the nodewise rectangular upper variance endpoint into unconditional conservative design-based coverage once the adaptive predictable quadratic variation stabilizes relative to its own design expectation.
statements.gap: Saco2026SelfNormalizedAdaptiveExperiments, Assumption 5.11, imposes a high-probability linear lower bound on predictable quadratic variation under iid arrivals, while Theorem 5.14 studentizes by realized quadratic variation. LiZhao2026AdaptiveDesignBased, Section 5, Definition 2, and Theorem 6 use a generally conservative covariance estimator after the earlier Theorem 5. statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D\), and take probability and expectation under its original sequential randomization law. By \(\mathrm{def:aipw\text{-}estimator}\), consistency, \(p_{nba}=m_{nba}/n_{nb}\), and the fixed causal estimand, direct subtraction gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n
&=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}w_{nb}\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_a
\left\{\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}
\mathbf1\{Z_{nbi}=a\}R_{nbi}(a)-\bar R_{nba}\right\}\\
&=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}D_{nb}=M_{nB_n}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]
The martingale conclusion of \(\mathrm{thm:exact\text{-}predictable\text{-}ot\text{-}envelope}\) shows that \((D_{nb})_{b\le B_n}\) is a square-integrable martingale-difference array. In particular, cross-block covariances vanish by iterated expectation without conditioning on the terminal adaptive history.

We derive the conditional Lindeberg condition from the primitive residual-moment and block-leverage assumptions. Conditional on \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\), put
\[
x_i(a)=R_{nbi}(a)-\bar R_{nba},
\qquad
X_a=\frac1{m_{nba}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal U_{nb}}
\mathbf1\{Z_{nbi}=a\}x_i(a).
\]
Then \(D_{nb}=w_{nb}\sum_ac_aX_a\). The power-mean inequality, Jensen's inequality, and \(\mathrm{ass:residual\text{-}moments}\) imply
\[
\frac1{n_{nb}}\sum_i|x_i(a)|^4
\le16\frac1{n_{nb}}\sum_i|R_{nbi}(a)|^4
\le16\left\{\frac1{n_{nb}}\sum_i|R_{nbi}(a)|^{4+\delta_0}\right\}^{4/(4+\delta_0)}
\le16C_R^{4/(4+\delta_0)}.
\tag{2}
\]

We now derive the needed fourth-moment sampling bound. Let \(x_1,\ldots,x_N\) be any centered list, let \(S\) be a uniformly chosen subset of size \(m\), define \(A_r=\sum_{i=1}^Nx_i^r\), and let \(\pi_r=(m)_r/(N)_r\), with \(\pi_r=0\) if \(r>m\). Expansion according to the index-multiplicity patterns \(4\), \(3+1\), \(2+2\), \(2+1+1\), and \(1+1+1+1\), using \(\sum_ix_i=0\), gives
\[
E\left(\sum_{i\in S}x_i\right)^4
=\{\pi_1-7\pi_2+12\pi_3-6\pi_4\}A_4
+3\{\pi_2-2\pi_3+\pi_4\}A_2^2.
\tag{3}
\]
For completeness, the five contributions are respectively
\[
\pi_1A_4,\quad -4\pi_2A_4,\quad
3\pi_2(A_2^2-A_4),\quad
6\pi_3(2A_4-A_2^2),\quad
\pi_4(3A_2^2-6A_4).
\]
Since \(0\le\pi_r\le1\), \(A_2^2\le NA_4\), and \(m\ge\varepsilon_0N\), (3) implies
\[
E\left(\frac1m\sum_{i\in S}x_i\right)^4
\le\left(\frac{26}{\varepsilon_0}+\frac{12}{\varepsilon_0^2}\right)
\frac1{m^2}\frac{A_4}{N}.
\tag{4}
\]
Under complete-block randomization, the marginal arm-\(a\) sample is such a uniform subset; overlap gives \(m_{nba}\ge\varepsilon_0n_{nb}\). Combining (2)--(4), \(\sum_ac_a^2=1\), and
\[
\left(\sum_ac_aX_a\right)^4
\le\left(\sum_aX_a^2\right)^2
\le K\sum_aX_a^4
\]
produces a constant \(C_0<\infty\), depending only on \(K,\varepsilon_0,\delta_0,C_R\), such that
\[
E(D_{nb}^4\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
\le C_0\left(\frac{w_{nb}^2}{n_{nb}}\right)^2
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{5}
\]

Define the deterministic, array-specific scale
\[
\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}^2=E_{\mathbb D}V_n.
\]
Martingale orthogonality and (1) give
\(\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}^2=\operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb D}(M_{nB_n})\), while \(\mathrm{ass:qv\text{-}growth}\) gives
\[
\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}^2\ge v_0s_n^2>0.
\tag{6}
\]
Writing \(t_{nb}=w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}\), equations (5)--(6), \(\sum_bt_{nb}=s_n^2\), and \(\mathrm{ass:block\text{-}leverage}\) yield
\[
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}
\frac{\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}E_{\mathbb D}D_{nb}^4}{\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}^4}
\le\frac{C_0}{v_0^2}\frac{\sum_bt_{nb}^2}{s_n^4}
\le\frac{C_0}{v_0^2}\ell_n\longrightarrow0.
\tag{7}
\]
For \(\epsilon>0\), set
\[
\Lambda_{n,\mathbb D}(\epsilon)
=\frac1{\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}^2}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}
E_{\mathbb D}\left[D_{nb}^2\mathbf1\{|D_{nb}|>\epsilon\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}\}
\middle|\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\right].
\]
The inequality \(u^2\mathbf1\{|u|>x\}\le u^4/x^2\), (7), and Markov's inequality imply
\[
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}E_{\mathbb D}\Lambda_{n,\mathbb D}(\epsilon)
\le\frac1{\epsilon^2}
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}
\frac{\sum_bE_{\mathbb D}D_{nb}^4}{\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}^4}
\longrightarrow0.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus the conditional Lindeberg condition holds uniformly in probability.

The established martingale central limit theorem
\(\mathrm{lem:martingale\text{-}clt\text{-}predictable\text{-}variation}\) applies because (8) supplies its Lindeberg premise and \(\mathrm{ass:qv\text{-}stabilization}\) supplies
\[
\frac{V_n}{\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}^2}
=\frac{V_n}{E_{\mathbb D}V_n}\longrightarrow1
\quad\text{in probability, uniformly over }\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D.
\tag{9}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}}
\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)
\quad\text{uniformly over }\mathfrak D.
\tag{10}
\]
To justify the asserted uniformity, suppose it failed. Then some subsequence and choices \(\mathbb D_n\in\mathfrak D\) would retain a fixed distributional discrepancy. Selecting row \(n\) from \(\mathbb D_n\) forms one diagonal martingale triangular array. The common bounds (8)--(9) hold for this diagonal array, so the cited martingale theorem forces Gaussian convergence, a contradiction.

On the event \(|V_n/\sigma_{n,\mathbb D}^2-1|\le\zeta\), the statistic normalized by \(\sqrt{V_n}\) is sandwiched between deterministic rescalings of the statistic in (10) by \(\sqrt{1-\zeta}\) and \(\sqrt{1+\zeta}\). Equations (9)--(10), continuity of the Gaussian distribution function, and then \(\zeta\downarrow0\) prove
\[
T_{n,\mathbb D}:=\frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sqrt{V_n}}
\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)
\quad\text{uniformly over }\mathfrak D.
\tag{11}
\]

It remains to prove conservative studentization. The exact envelope gives \(V_n\le U_n\) pathwise. Since \(r_n=q_n^{-\kappa}\to0\), \(\mathrm{thm:history\text{-}uniform\text{-}plugin}\) and \(V_n\ge v_0s_n^2\) imply, for every fixed \(\eta\in(0,1)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}
\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{|\widehat U_n-U_n|>\eta V_n\}
&\le\sup_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}
\Pr_{\mathbb D}\left\{\frac{|\widehat U_n-U_n|}{s_n^2}>\eta v_0\right\}\\
&\le\frac{C_{\mathrm{ep}}r_n}{1\wedge(\eta v_0)}\longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
On the complementary event,
\[
\widehat U_n\ge U_n-\eta V_n\ge(1-\eta)V_n.
\tag{13}
\]
Let \(A_{n,\mathbb D}(\eta)=\{|\widehat U_n-U_n|\le\eta V_n\}\). By \(\mathrm{def:wald\text{-}interval}\) and (13),
\[
\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{\tau_n\in\mathrm{CI}_{n,1-\alpha}\}
\ge\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{|T_{n,\mathbb D}|\le z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{1-\eta}\}
-\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{A_{n,\mathbb D}(\eta)^c\}.
\]
Equations (11)--(12) and continuity of \(\Phi\) give
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb D\in\mathfrak D}
\Pr_{\mathbb D}\{\tau_n\in\mathrm{CI}_{n,1-\alpha}\}
\ge2\Phi\!\left(z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{1-\eta}\right)-1.
\tag{14}
\]
Letting \(\eta\downarrow0\) proves the lower bound \(1-\alpha\). The deterministic normalization \(E_{\mathbb D}V_n\) may depend on the array, and no common limit for \(E_{\mathbb D}V_n/s_n^2\) was used. All coverage probabilities are unconditional under the original adaptive design.

statements.statement:
For each \(n\), define, within this statement,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 A_n&=\sup_{\varpi\in\mathcal P_n}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}
 \frac{w_{nb}^2}{s_n^2(n_{nb}-1)}\left[
 \inf_{\gamma\in\mathcal I_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi)}}\int\left(\sum_ac_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma-J_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi),-}\right],\\
 C_n&=\inf_{\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)}\sup_{\varpi\in\mathcal P_n}
 \sum_{b=1}^{B_n}\frac{w_{nb}^2}{s_n^2(n_{nb}-1)}\left[
 \int\left(\sum_ac_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma_{nb}^{\Xi,h_b(\varpi)}
 -\inf_{\gamma\in\mathcal I_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi)}}\int\left(\sum_ac_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma\right].
 \end{aligned}
\]
Whenever \(\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\ne\varnothing\),
\[
 \max\{A_n,C_n\}\le\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\le A_n+C_n,
 \qquad
 \Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\le A_n\le B_n\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n).
\]
Consequently, \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\to0\) if and only if \(A_n\to0\) and \(C_n\to0\).  The quantity \(A_n\) is the computable root-to-leaf accumulation of the single-node multi-index integrality losses, while \(C_n\) is the infimum of the worst-path residual cross-history loss from requiring one fixed potential-outcome array, common unit labels, and one predictable fitting rule.  The decomposition reduces global simultaneous history-tree attainment to controlling \(C_n\), but makes no general claim that \(C_n\to0\).

As a counterexample to inferring nondegenerate admissible attainment from zero gap, suppose for every \(n\) that \(\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\ne\varnothing\) and every nodewise centered margin is \(\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\).  Then \(A_n=C_n=\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=0\), but every completion has \(V_n=0\) and hence violates \(\mathrm{ass:qv\text{-}growth}\).  Thus this global history-tree compatibility obstruction is logically separate from any minimax fixed-fraction upper-endpoint converse on a nonadaptive fixed-quota subclass.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\) and suppose \(\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\ne\varnothing\).  By the definitions of \(w_{nb}\) and \(s_n^2\), each \(w_{nb}>0\) and
\[
s_n^2=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}\frac{w_{nb}^2}{n_{nb}}>0.
\]
The predictable counts satisfy \(1\le m_{nba}^{h}\le n_{nb}-1\), so \(n_{nb}-1>0\).  Therefore the coefficient
\[
d_{nb}:=\frac{w_{nb}^2}{s_n^2(n_{nb}-1)}
\]
is well defined and strictly positive.  For a coupling \(\gamma\) define the nonnegative quadratic cost
\[
\Phi(\gamma):=\int\left(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_ax_a\right)^2d\gamma.
\]
At a node \((b,h)\), set
\[
 r_{nb}^{h}:=d_{nb}\left\{\inf_{\gamma\in\mathcal I_{nb}^{h}}\Phi(\gamma)-J_{nb}^{h,-}\right\}
\]
and, for \(\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\), set
\[
 t_{nb}^{\Xi,h}:=d_{nb}\left\{\Phi(\gamma_{nb}^{\Xi,h})-\inf_{\gamma\in\mathcal I_{nb}^{h}}\Phi(\gamma)\right\}.
\]

We first establish the signs.  Each \(\mu_{nba}^{h}\) is an empirical law of \(n_{nb}\) centered residuals indexed by \(i\in\mathcal U_{nb}\).  Pairing the atoms with the same index in every arm produces at least one deterministic label-matching coupling, so \(\mathcal I_{nb}^{h}\ne\varnothing\).  By the declared meaning of \(\mathcal I_{nb}^{h}\), every member of this finite matching set is a coupling of the prescribed margins, and hence
\(\mathcal I_{nb}^{h}\subseteq\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\).  Definition \(\text{def:history-tree-rectangular-relaxation}\) gives
\[
J_{nb}^{h,-}=\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma_{nb}^{h}}\Phi(\gamma)
\le \inf_{\gamma\in\mathcal I_{nb}^{h}}\Phi(\gamma),
\]
so \(r_{nb}^{h}\ge0\).  Definition \(\text{def:completion-class}\) says that \(\gamma_{nb}^{\Xi,h}\) is induced by the common unit labels of \(\Xi_n\).  It is therefore one of the deterministic label-matching couplings in \(\mathcal I_{nb}^{h}\), whence
\[
\inf_{\gamma\in\mathcal I_{nb}^{h}}\Phi(\gamma)
\le \Phi(\gamma_{nb}^{\Xi,h})
\]
and \(t_{nb}^{\Xi,h}\ge0\).

The declared formulas for \(U_{nb}^{h}\) and \(Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h}\) have the same diagonal term.  Subtracting them, and then dividing by the positive number \(s_n^2\), gives the exact nodewise identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{U_{nb}^{h}-Q_{nb}^{\Xi,h}}{s_n^2}
&=d_{nb}\left\{\Phi(\gamma_{nb}^{\Xi,h})-J_{nb}^{h,-}\right\}\\
&=r_{nb}^{h}+t_{nb}^{\Xi,h}.
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(\varpi\in\mathcal P_n\), define
\[
R_n(\varpi):=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}r_{nb}^{h_b(\varpi)},
\qquad
T_n^{\Xi}(\varpi):=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}t_{nb}^{\Xi,h_b(\varpi)}.
\]
The preceding identity and Definition \(\text{def:completion-gap}\) now yield, without conditioning on a realized terminal path,
\[
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)
=\inf_{\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)}
 \sup_{\varpi\in\mathcal P_n}
 \{R_n(\varpi)+T_n^{\Xi}(\varpi)\}.
\]
By their displayed definitions in the statement,
\[
A_n=\sup_{\varpi\in\mathcal P_n}R_n(\varpi),
\qquad
C_n=\inf_{\Xi_n\in\mathcal C_n(\boldsymbol\mu_n)}
     \sup_{\varpi\in\mathcal P_n}T_n^{\Xi}(\varpi).
\]

Because \(R_n\ge0\) and \(T_n^{\Xi}\ge0\), for every completion \(\Xi_n\),
\[
\sup_{\varpi}\{R_n(\varpi)+T_n^{\Xi}(\varpi)\}
\ge \sup_{\varpi}R_n(\varpi)=A_n
\]
and
\[
\sup_{\varpi}\{R_n(\varpi)+T_n^{\Xi}(\varpi)\}
\ge \sup_{\varpi}T_n^{\Xi}(\varpi).
\]
Taking the infimum over the nonempty completion class in the first and second inequalities gives, respectively,
\[
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\ge A_n,
\qquad
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\ge C_n.
\]
For the reverse bound, the elementary supremum inequality gives, for each \(\Xi_n\),
\[
\sup_{\varpi}\{R_n(\varpi)+T_n^{\Xi}(\varpi)\}
\le \sup_{\varpi}R_n(\varpi)+\sup_{\varpi}T_n^{\Xi}(\varpi)
=A_n+\sup_{\varpi}T_n^{\Xi}(\varpi).
\]
Taking the infimum over \(\Xi_n\) yields
\[
\max\{A_n,C_n\}\le
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)
\le A_n+C_n.
\]

By Definition \(\text{def:completion-gap}\),
\[
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)
=\sup_{b\le B_n,\,h\in\mathcal H_{n,b-1}}r_{nb}^{h}.
\]
Every node in the universal history tree lies on at least one root-to-leaf path.  Since every \(r_{nb}^{h}\ge0\), if a path \(\varpi\) passes through \(h\) before block \(b\), then
\[
r_{nb}^{h}\le R_n(\varpi)\le A_n.
\]
Taking the supremum over nodes proves
\(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\le A_n\).  Conversely, every root-to-leaf path has exactly \(B_n\) summands and each is at most \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\), so
\[
R_n(\varpi)\le B_n\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n).
\]
Taking the supremum over \(\varpi\) proves
\[
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)
\le A_n\le B_n\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n).
\]

All three quantities in the first sandwich are nonnegative.  Hence \(A_n\to0\) and \(C_n\to0\) imply \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\to0\) by the upper bound, while \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)\to0\) implies both \(A_n\to0\) and \(C_n\to0\) by the two lower bounds.

We make the computability claim explicit.  At a fixed node enumerate the atoms of arm \(a\), with multiplicity, as \(x_{a1},\ldots,x_{a n_{nb}}\).  The value \(J_{nb}^{h,-}\) is the optimum of the finite linear program with variables \(q_{r_1,\ldots,r_K}\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{minimize}_{q}\quad
 &\sum_{r_1=1}^{n_{nb}}\cdots\sum_{r_K=1}^{n_{nb}}
 q_{r_1,\ldots,r_K}
 \left(\sum_{a=1}^{K}c_ax_{a r_a}\right)^2,\\
\operatorname{subject\ to}\quad
 &q_{r_1,\ldots,r_K}\ge0,\\
 &\sum_{(r_j)_{j\ne a}}q_{r_1,\ldots,r_K}=\frac1{n_{nb}}
 \quad\text{for every }a\in\mathcal A\text{ and }r_a\in\{1,\ldots,n_{nb}\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Indeed, every feasible array induces a coupling of the empirical margins, and every such coupling can be lifted to a feasible array by splitting the mass attached to repeated atom values uniformly among their labels.  Thus the program has exactly the feasible costs in \(\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\).  In addition, \(\mathcal P_n\) and every nonempty \(\mathcal I_{nb}^{h}\) are finite by their declared types.  Hence the matching infimum is a finite minimum, each \(r_{nb}^{h}\) is computable from a finite linear program and a finite enumeration, and \(A_n\) is a finite maximum of finite sums.  The exact pathwise equality \(R_n+T_n^{\Xi}\) identifies \(C_n\) as the residual term after imposing one globally compatible completion.

It remains to verify the counterexample and its boundary.  Suppose for every \(n\) that the completion class is nonempty and \(\mu_{nba}^{h}=\delta_{0_{\mathbb R}}\) at every \((b,h,a)\).  The only coupling of these point masses is \(\delta_{(0,\ldots,0)}\); it belongs both to \(\Gamma_{nb}^{h}\) and to \(\mathcal I_{nb}^{h}\), and its cost is zero.  Consequently
\[
J_{nb}^{h,-}=0,
\qquad
r_{nb}^{h}=0,
\qquad
t_{nb}^{\Xi,h}=0
\]
for every node and every completion.  The definitions then give
\[
A_n=C_n=\Delta_n^{\mathrm{tree}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)
=\Delta_n^{\mathrm{node}}(\boldsymbol\mu_n)=0.
\]
The point-mass margin also implies, unit by unit,
\[
R_{nbi}^{h}(a)-\bar R_{nba}^{h}=0.
\]
At the realized pre-block history this says that every armwise residual is constant across the block.  Since every \(m_{nba}>0\), the sampled residual mean equals the full residual mean for every assignment.  Definition \(\text{def:block-martingale}\) therefore gives \(D_{nb}=0\) in every block, and hence
\[
V_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})=0.
\]
On the other hand, \(v_0>0\) by its declared type and \(s_n^2>0\), so \(0<v_0s_n^2\).  Thus \(V_n=0\) violates \(\text{ass:qv-growth}\).  This proves that a zero global completion gap does not by itself provide a nondegenerate admissible near-attaining sequence, while making no assertion against a separate fixed-quota subclass converse.

statements.statement: For two equally weighted finite empirical margins on \(\mathbb R\) and the contrast \(c=(1,-1)/\sqrt2\), the minimum of \(\frac12E(X_1-X_2)^2\) over all couplings is attained by equal-rank pairing and the maximum is attained by reverse-rank pairing; equivalently, the two quantile formulas in \(\mathrm{def:twoarm\text{-}sorting}\) equal \(J_{nb}^{-}\) and \(J_{nb}^{+}\).

Let \((D_{nb})_{b\le B_n}\) be a triangular array of square-integrable martingale differences with respect to the pre-increment histories \(\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\), let \(V_n=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})\), and put \(\sigma_n^2=E(V_n)>0\).  If \(V_n/\sigma_n^2\to1\) in probability and, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
\frac1{\sigma_n^2}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}E\left[D_{nb}^2\mathbf 1\{|D_{nb}|>\epsilon\sigma_n\}\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1}\right]\to0
\quad\text{in probability},
\]
then \(\sigma_n^{-1}\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}D_{nb}\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\).

statements.statement:
There exists a nonadaptive fixed-quota subclass of an admissible common-parameter class \(\mathfrak D\) with \(B_n\to\infty\), \(q_n\to\infty\), equal block weights \(w_{nb}=B_n^{-1}\), block sizes \(n_{nb}=Kq_n\), equal quotas \(m_{nba}=q_n\), zero adjustments \(g_{nbi}(a)=0\), and identical bounded potential-outcome lists across arms, such that \(J_{nb}^{-}=0\) in every block and \(V_n=U_n\) deterministically. This subclass satisfies the full overlap, residual-moment, count-growth, block-leverage, predictable-QV growth, predictable-QV stabilization, endpoint-consistency, and martingale-CLT conditions. Consequently, for every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) and every fixed \(\rho\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n|\le z_{1-\alpha/2}
 \sqrt{(1-\rho)\widehat U_n}\right\}
 \longrightarrow
 2\Phi\!\left(z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{1-\rho}\right)-1
 <1-\alpha.
\]
Therefore, for any broader design family containing this subclass, the limsup of its worst-case coverage after replacing \(\widehat U_n\) by \((1-\rho)\widehat U_n\) is at most the displayed strict sub-nominal limit. This is a fixed-quota subclass converse for uniform inference, not a claim that independently selected nodewise transport optimizers are jointly realizable by one completion over an adaptive history tree.
statements.justification: An explicit admissible fixed-quota sequence makes the transport upper endpoint equal the true predictable quadratic variation and supplies a matching fixed-fraction undercoverage certificate.
statements.gap: Nodewise completion attainability is not needed for this inference converse; the remaining unsolved issue is simultaneous compatibility across an adaptive history tree.
statements.consumer: The result certifies that a batched quota-controlled trial cannot uniformly shorten the transport-based standard error by any fixed fraction, even on the simplest nonadaptive subfamily.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(K\ge2\) and a contrast \(c\) satisfying \(\sum_ac_a=0\) and \(\sum_ac_a^2=1\). Define
\[
B_n=n,\qquad q_n=2n,\qquad n_{nb}=Kq_n=2Kn,
\qquad m_{nba}=q_n,qquad w_{nb}=B_n^{-1}.
\tag{1}
\]
In every block label the units by \(i=1,\ldots,2Kn\), and set
\[
x_{nbi}=\begin{cases}-1,&i\le Kn,\\1,&i>Kn,\end{cases}
\qquad
Y_{nbi}(a)=x_{nbi},qquad g_{nbi}(a)=0
\quad(a\in\mathcal A).
\tag{2}
\]
The subclass consists of this construction and arbitrary deterministic within-block permutations of the balanced list, using the same permutation in every arm of a block. In each block, conditional on the past, assign uniformly over allocations having exactly \(q_n\) units in every arm. Thus counts and adjustments are deterministic and predictable, all potential outcomes are fixed before randomization, consistency defines the observed response, and assignment is the only source of randomness.

We verify membership in one common-parameter class. Take
\[
\varepsilon_0=\frac1{2K},\qquad \delta_0=1,
\qquad C_R=1,qquad v_0=K,qquad \ell_n=\frac1n.
\]
Since \(p_{nba}=1/K\),
\[
\varepsilon_0\le p_{nba}\le1-(K-1)\varepsilon_0.
\]
The residuals equal \(x_{nbi}\), so
\(n_{nb}^{-1}\sum_i|R_{nbi}(a)|^{4+\delta_0}=1=C_R\). The minimum arm count is \(q_n=2n\to\infty\). Also \(N_n=B_nKq_n\), whence
\[
s_n^2=\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}\frac{w_{nb}^2}{n_{nb}}
=\frac1{B_nKq_n},
\qquad
\frac{w_{nb}^2/n_{nb}}{s_n^2}
=\frac1{B_n}=\ell_n\longrightarrow0.
\tag{3}
\]
The two contrast restrictions hold by construction. This verifies every member property of \(\mathrm{def:admissible\text{-}arrays}\) except predictable-QV growth, which is checked below.

The residual mean in every arm and block is zero, and the common finite-population variance is
\[
S_{nba}^2=S_n^2=\frac{Kq_n}{Kq_n-1}.
\tag{4}
\]
The diagonal coupling \((X_1,\ldots,X_K)=(X,\ldots,X)\), with \(X\) uniform on the balanced list in (2), lies in \(\Gamma_{nb}\). Since \(\sum_ac_a=0\), its cost is
\[
E\left(\sum_ac_aX_a\right)^2
=E\left(X\sum_ac_a\right)^2=0.
\]
The cost is nonnegative, so \(J_{nb}^{-}=0\). The true common-label coupling is this diagonal coupling. The conditional-variance identity in
\(\mathrm{thm:exact\text{-}predictable\text{-}ot\text{-}envelope}\), together with \(\sum_ac_a^2=1\), gives
\[
E(D_{nb}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})
=U_{nb}=\frac{S_n^2}{B_n^2q_n},
\qquad
V_n=U_n=\frac{S_n^2}{B_nq_n}.
\tag{5}
\]
This quantity is deterministic. Equations (3)--(5) imply
\[
\frac{V_n}{s_n^2}=KS_n^2\ge K=v_0,
\qquad
\frac{V_n}{E V_n}=1.
\tag{6}
\]
Thus predictable-QV growth and predictable-QV stabilization hold uniformly over the subclass, the latter exactly.

The smallest arithmetic witness is the case \(K=2\), \(n=1\), for which the block list is \(\{-1,-1,1,1\}\). With unnormalized contrast \((1,-1)\), diagonal pairing gives squared contrast zero at every atom, while reverse pairing gives squared contrast four at every atom. Thus the two transport costs are \(0\) and \(4\). With the required normalized contrast \((1,-1)/\sqrt2\), both costs are divided by two. This exactly checks the endpoint direction and confirms nontrivial width.

By \(\mathrm{thm:history\text{-}uniform\text{-}plugin}\),
\(\widehat U_n-U_n=o_{\Pr}(s_n^2)\) under the original randomization. Since (4)--(6) give \(U_n/s_n^2=KS_n^2\to K>0\),
\[
\frac{\widehat U_n}{V_n}=\frac{\widehat U_n}{U_n}\longrightarrow1
\quad\text{in probability}.
\tag{7}
\]

We verify the martingale CLT from the primitives. Estimator algebra, consistency, and \(p_{nba}=m_{nba}/n_{nb}\) give \(\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n=M_{nB_n}\). For an arm sample mean
\(X_a=q_n^{-1}\sum_{i:Z_{nbi}=a}x_{nbi}\), the fourth-moment expansion by inclusion multiplicities, with \(N=Kq_n\), \(A_2=A_4=N\), and \(\pi_j=(q_n)_j/(N)_j\), gives
\[
E(q_nX_a)^4
=\{\pi_1-7\pi_2+12\pi_3-6\pi_4\}A_4
+3\{\pi_2-2\pi_3+\pi_4\}A_2^2
\le26N+12N^2.
\]
Hence \(E(X_a^4\mid\mathcal F_{n,b-1})\le C_Kq_n^{-2}\). Since
\(D_{nb}=B_n^{-1}\sum_ac_aX_a\), \(\sum_ac_a^2=1\), and
\((\sum_ac_aX_a)^4\le K\sum_aX_a^4\),
\[
\sum_{b=1}^{B_n}ED_{nb}^4
\le\frac{C_K}{B_n^3q_n^2},
\qquad
\frac{\sum_bED_{nb}^4}{V_n^2}
\le\frac{C_K}{B_n(S_n^2)^2}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{8}
\]
For every \(\epsilon>0\), the conditional Lindeberg sum divided by \(V_n\) has expectation at most \(\epsilon^{-2}\sum_bED_{nb}^4/V_n^2\), by
\(u^2\mathbf1\{|u|>x\}\le u^4/x^2\). It converges to zero in probability by Markov's inequality. Together with \(V_n/EV_n=1\), the established martingale central limit theorem
\(\mathrm{lem:martingale\text{-}clt\text{-}predictable\text{-}variation}\) gives
\[
T_n:=\frac{\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n}{\sqrt{V_n}}
\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\tag{9}
\]
The causal estimand remains distinct from this randomization limit: indeed,
\(\tau_n=0\), because every unit's fixed causal contrast is
\(x_{nbi}\sum_ac_a=0\).

For fixed \(\rho\in(0,1)\), the shortened interval covers exactly when
\[
|T_n|\le z_{1-\alpha/2}
\sqrt{(1-\rho)\widehat U_n/V_n}.
\]
On the event \(|\widehat U_n/V_n-1|\le\zeta\), its coverage probability is sandwiched, up to the probability of the complementary event, between the probabilities that \(|T_n|\) is at most
\(z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{(1-\rho)(1-\zeta)}\) and
\(z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{(1-\rho)(1+\zeta)}\). Equations (7)--(9), continuity of \(\Phi\), and then \(\zeta\downarrow0\) yield
\[
\Pr\!\left\{|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_n|\le z_{1-\alpha/2}
\sqrt{(1-\rho)\widehat U_n}\right\}
\longrightarrow
2\Phi\!\left(z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{1-\rho}\right)-1.
\tag{10}
\]
Because \(z_{1-\alpha/2}>0\), \(0<\sqrt{1-\rho}<1\), and \(\Phi\) is strictly increasing, the limit in (10) is strictly below
\(2\Phi(z_{1-\alpha/2})-1=1-\alpha\).

Finally, if a broader design family contains this subclass, its worst-case coverage is no larger than coverage on the constructed member. Taking \(\limsup\) and applying (10) gives the stated matching fixed-fraction undercoverage certificate. The witness is nonadaptive and fixed-quota, so this inference necessity result does not assert cross-history compatibility of independently selected nodewise transport optimizers.

Let \(K\ge2\), let \(c\in\mathbb R^K\), and let \(
u_1,\ldots,
u_K\) be finitely supported probability measures on \(\mathbb R\). Write \(\Gamma(
u_1,\ldots,
u_K)\) for their coupling set. For the quadratic cost \(q(x_1,\ldots,x_K)=(\sum_{a=1}^Kc_ax_a)^2\),
\[
\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma(
u_1,\ldots,
u_K)}\int q\,d\gamma
=\sup_{\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_K:\,\sum_{a=1}^K\phi_a(x_a)\le q(x_1,\ldots,x_K)}
\sum_{a=1}^K\int\phi_a\,d
u_a.
\]
Equivalently, after labeling the support atoms, the finite coupling LP and its finite Kantorovich dual have the same optimal value.

sampling_model.design: The paper restricts attention to sequential complete randomization within blocks: integer arm quotas are chosen from the pre-block history and assignments are then uniform over allocations realizing those quotas. This is implementable by batched platforms that update quotas between batches and enforce minimum cells or capacity caps; it is a restriction of, rather than a condition supplied by, the broader Li--Zhao block-adaptive framework.
sampling_model.units: A triangular array of fixed finite populations partitioned into growing, disjoint blocks.
sampling_model.treatment: A fixed number \(K\) of arms and a prespecified normalized contrast \(c\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every predictable arm fraction obeys the same constant \(\varepsilon_0\) over arrays and histories.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Armwise outcome adjustments are fit from past blocks only and held fixed within the current block. Each plug-in transport margin uses only assigned-arm observations and is centered by that arm's observed residual sample mean; the common nuisance-residual moment envelope is \((\delta_0,C_R)\).
sampling_model.uniformity: The number of arms \(K\), overlap and moment constants, deterministic lower count sequence \(q_n\), leverage envelope \(\ell_n\), and QV lower constant \(v_0\) are common across \(\mathfrak D\).
sampling_model.randomness: The only randomness is sequential treatment assignment; potential outcomes are fixed.
sampling_model.terminal_conditioning: All guarantees are unconditional under the sequential design and use only pre-block conditioning; the realized final adaptive path is never frozen.

estimand_functional: \(V_n\in[L_n,U_n]\), with \(L_n\) and \(U_n\) the block-weighted multi-marginal transport functionals in \(\text{def:qv-envelope}\), estimated by \([\widehat L_n,\widehat U_n]\)
